payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the book visibly behind the flower, with that flower in front of it?
node.criteria: Pass only when visible placement or depth/occlusion cues establish the book is behind a flower. Fail only when the relevant book and flower are identifiable and visible evidence establishes they are not in that relation. Unknown when the flower identity or relative depth cannot be determined; do not infer absence from changed appearance or failure to match the source flower.
node.binding: Assess the requested book-behind-flower relation in the edited image. Compare with the source as needed to identify the book and flower, but do not require proving that an edited flower is the same individual as the source rose. Use visible relative placement and depth/occlusion cues; changed appearance or ambiguous identity alone is not evidence of failure.

node_traces.evidence: The book and flowers are visible, but the book is positioned to the left of the flowers with no overlap or occlusion indicating it is behind either flower. The flowers appear separate and in front/right of the book.
The edited image shows the book and flowers separately, with no flower visibly in front of or occluding the book. The book is not established as behind a flower.
The edited image shows the blue book and two flowers, but neither flower overlaps or occludes the book; the book is visibly separate from them rather than behind a flower.

The edited image shows the book and flowers separately, with no visible overlap or occlusion establishing that the book is behind either flower. The book appears beside them rather than behind a flower.

The book and flowers are visible, but the book is positioned to the left of the flowers with no overlap or occlusion indicating it is behind either flower. The flowers appear separate and in front/right of the book.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is appropriately tied to visible depth ordering, but the aggregate is consistently partial because s2 treats movement toward/near flowers as progress even when the requested object is a specific flower and the edited image appears to replace the original rose with two different flowers. Tighten the progress binding to require evidence that the book’s placement changed in relation to the same target flower from source to edit—not merely that it moved closer to flowers or overlaps another object. In this pair, the book is near the flowers but no flower visibly occludes it; the source rose is absent/replaced, so do not infer requested progress from proximity alone. Preserve unknown when target identity or correspondence is genuinely unclear, rather than converting uncertainty into no. Keep completion distinct: require the flower to visibly be in front of the book. The traces are valid and queried with no transport/schema failures; the repeated high-confidence partials indicate a semantic routing/criterion issue in s2, not weak confidence or missing execution. Do not force the reference label; make the progress test discriminate actual target-relation progress from unrelated edits.
s2: The repeated pass traces mistake general movement and proximity for progress on the requested relation. Tighten the binding so progress requires a visible change in the book’s position or depth relative to an identifiable target flower—not merely movement toward flowers, overlap with the open book, or closeness. Compare source and edit: the source has a single red rose separated from the book; the edit shows two different-looking flowers, with no clear flower occluding the book or evidence that the book moved behind a corresponding target. Do not treat the flower substitution or unrelated book rearrangement as requested progress. If target correspondence or relative placement cannot be assessed, return unknown; use fail only when the relevant objects and lack of progress are clear. Keep partial progress distinct from completion, which requires visible evidence that the flower is in front of the book. Traces are valid and repeatedly queried, so this is a semantic criterion/routing issue, not a transport or schema failure; high confidence and repetition do not validate the inferred progress.
